structured_output.steelman: The strongest reading: students open myNXU rarely because the dashboard gives them no reason to return between Canvas sessions, so the CEO wants the landing view to surface something students act on each login, measured by return visits. That reading is constructed, not stated — the spec names no problem, no metric, no segment and no observation that prompted it, so it is underspecified on its own terms.

ambiguities.text: What 'engage more' means and how it is measured: return visits per week, distinct login days, actions taken from the dashboard, time-to-act on a deadline — and the current baseline.
ambiguities.why_it_bites_mid_build: Every candidate change (deadline summary, progress widget, referral nudge, streaks) targets a different metric; without one, the team builds a guess and cannot tell if it worked.

ambiguities.text: What prompted the request — what did you see (analytics, a student complaint, a board question, a competitor) that says the dashboard is the problem rather than notifications, Canvas or the mobile experience?
ambiguities.why_it_bites_mid_build: The observation decides the surface. If students never reach the dashboard, redesigning it moves nothing; the fix is an email or push, which is a different spec.

ambiguities.text: Which students: all, new starters in their first month, learners in SAP warning/probation, learners with open invoices, or learners between terms?
ambiguities.why_it_bites_mid_build: The content that brings a first-month starter back (next assignment, ID upload deadline) differs from what brings back a between-terms learner (course selection window, invoice). One dashboard cannot lead with both.

ambiguities.text: 'Something that makes them want to come back' — which content: the next dated items from the deadline rail, course progress from Canvas, grades, wallet/referral credit, a Nexa prompt?
ambiguities.why_it_bites_mid_build: The team can settle this in the room once the metric and segment are fixed, but the choice sets size: rail events are available today; module-level progress from Canvas is unknown.

ambiguities.text: 'Modern and clean' has no owner or sign-off. Is the designer's approved mock the criterion, or does the CEO review?
ambiguities.why_it_bites_mid_build: Without a named approver, visual work loops indefinitely at the end of the sprint.

ambiguities.text: Design section says 'n/a — no UI' for a dashboard change and Dependencies says 'None'. Both are wrong on their face; the spec needs the designer's name in it.
ambiguities.why_it_bites_mid_build: An engineer picks this up believing there is no design work and no Canvas or analytics dependency, then blocks in week one.

untestable_criteria.criterion: THE SYSTEM SHALL make the dashboard more engaging for students.
untestable_criteria.rewrite: Within four weeks of release, the share of active students who open the dashboard on ≥ 3 distinct days per week rises from [baseline]% to [target]%, measured from myNXU page-view events.

untestable_criteria.criterion: WHEN a student logs in, THE SYSTEM SHALL show them something that makes them want to come back.
untestable_criteria.rewrite: WHEN a student logs in, THE SYSTEM SHALL show their next three dated items (assignment due, invoice due, document deadline, registration window) from the deadline rail, nearest first, above the fold on mobile and desktop; 7-day return rate after first login rises from [baseline]% to [target]%.

untestable_criteria.criterion: THE SYSTEM SHALL look modern and clean.
untestable_criteria.rewrite: The shipped dashboard matches the designer's approved mock [link] at 360px and 1280px widths; the designer signs off before the story moves to Done.

hidden_dependencies.name: Dashboard analytics / instrumentation
hidden_dependencies.why: The platform context lists no product analytics. Without a baseline for dashboard visits or actions, 'engage more' cannot be measured, and adding instrumentation may be the first sprint of work before any redesign.

hidden_dependencies.name: Canvas via LTI
hidden_dependencies.why: Any 'progress' or 'what to do next in your course' widget depends on Canvas data; item-level module completion readability from myNXU is unknown. If the chosen content needs it, the size jumps from S/M to XL.

hidden_dependencies.name: Deadline rail events
hidden_dependencies.why: The events available today (assignment due, grade posted, credential earned, invoice, document status, registration window) are the only material the dashboard can show without new integrations. The spec should name them as its bound.

size.risk: Unsizeable as written. If the requester pins one metric and one segment and the change is bounded to existing rail events with a designer's mock, it collapses to S–M in one sprint; if it requires Canvas module progress or new analytics, it stays XL.

refinement_agenda: Fix the single engagement metric, its baseline and target, and confirm the team can measure it today or name the instrumentation story that comes first.
Choose the one dashboard change most likely to move that metric for the named segment, bounded to events myNXU already has; park anything needing Canvas module data.
Replace 'modern and clean' with designer sign-off on an approved mock, and rewrite the three acceptance criteria to the observable forms above.
structured_output.requester_message: Fadl — the dashboard request can't reach the team yet because it doesn't say what you've seen or what should change. Before Thursday triage, we need three things from you and only you: (1) what prompted this — the number, complaint or observation that says the dashboard is the problem; (2) the one measure you'd accept as proof it worked (e.g. students opening the dashboard three days a week, or acting on a deadline sooner), with whatever baseline you have; (3) which students you have in mind — new starters, learners at risk, learners with open invoices, or everyone. With those, the designer and an engineer can settle the rest in refinement. Two corrections to the draft: this is UI work, so the designer is on it, and it touches Canvas and analytics, so 'no dependencies' is wrong. Current sprint items are committed through sprint end; if this jumps the queue, one of them slides, and the team will name which at Thursday triage once we know the size. I can't give a delivery date until the metric is fixed — the same request is a week or a quarter depending on the answer.
